title: What Is Wire Bonding? A Beginner's Guide to the Back-End Process That Connects Chips and Substrates with Fine Metal Wire
excerpt: Wire bonding is a back-end process that electrically connects the electrode pads on a semiconductor chip to terminals on a substrate or lead frame with fine wire made of gold, copper, aluminum, or similar metals. This beginner's guide covers the basic flow, materials, quality points such as wire breaks, poor bonds, and shorts, and the terms you'll see in job postings.
